verdict:
KILL, and it is not close. This is the one name of the four where the benches agreed, the primary reads held, and no adjudicator refereeing was needed.

THE BRIEF ASKED FOR A COURT ON THREE 'RESOLVABLE' FACTS AND THE MOST VALUABLE ONE RESOLVED AGAINST IT BEFORE THE COURT SAT. The triage argued the market repriced ~$187M of equity against a $356.1M judgment without the docket facts being public, and that apportionment across co-defendants could 'change the equity math by multiples.' Red pulled the note. The judgment was entered against 'the defendants, which include us' - the registrant itself, ordered to pay - and the defendant set is JBG Smith plus four JBG affiliates plus one Plaza Construction affiliate. Five of six pockets are the issuer's own family. Apportionment recovers, at most, one external contractor's share. Relief now requires appellate reversal on an 18-30 month clock, not a docket fetch. Blue confirmed the note language verbatim and correctly trimmed one overreach: red wrote that the judgment binds the Company AND the Operating Partnership explicitly, where the note says 'us' and 'one of our subsidiary entities.' Immaterial - the registrant is a named defendant ordered to pay either way.

THE TAIL IS BIGGER THAN THE HEADLINE AND THE ACCRUAL IS ZERO. The contingencies note discloses a range of '$0 to the $356.1 million judgment, plus attorneys' fees' plus 'post-judgment interest that will accrue during the appeal' - and the plaintiff was represented by Williams and Connolly under a statute that shifts fees. Call the true tail $400M-plus against roughly $850M of unit-level equity. Red ran the Up-C check rather than assuming, and it holds: 58,575,671 common shares on the August-5 cover plus the 18.2% OP and LTIP non-controlling interest, so the ~$836M figure is unit-level with no aggregation artifact. Against that tail, a two-gap repricing of ~$187M is roughly 45-50% of the gross exposure. That is not obviously excessive. There is no dislocation edge to harvest - the market did the arithmetic.

AND THE ACCRUAL IS THE POSTURE, NOT THE INFORMATION. The company recorded no liability on an ENTERED judgment, calling loss not probable while publicly announcing an appeal. The brief treated that $0 as a fact to arbitrage. It is an aggressive accounting stance on a judgment that already exists, and it means the balance sheet as presented understates the claim rather than validating it.

BLUE'S TWO ADDITIONS BOTH CUT DEEPER. First, the formation-timing defense is void: the brief argued substantial completion predated JBGS's 2017 formation, but JBGS was formed by absorbing the legacy JBG entities and their obligations, and it is a named defendant today. Second - and this belongs in the sizing, not in a footnote - the contingencies note contains ZERO insurance-recovery language on a construction-defect-plus-misrepresentation judgment. On a $356M tail, silence where you would expect a coverage discussion is itself a datum.

EVEN A CLEAN LEGAL OUTCOME LEAVES NOTHING OWNABLE. Strip the litigation entirely and you still hold a REIT at 12.4x net debt to EBITDA with same-store NOI at -4.0%, new-lease effective rents at -9.5%, office 78.0% leased but only 75.4% occupied, and a dividend declared at $0.175 against Core FFO of $0.18 - about 1.0x on a metric that excludes recurring tenant improvements, leasing commissions and capex, so true AFFO coverage is below 1.0x. The October dividend decision is a live down-catalyst the brief omitted entirely. The buyback that shrank the count from 114M to 58.6M was leverage-funded and now competes directly with a supersedeas bond for the same $74.8M of cash and a revolver drawable only subject to covenants.

RESPONSE TAXONOMY: THIS GETS NO PRICE GATE. Blue is right and I am endorsing it explicitly. The finding is business risk plus an unbounded legal tail running to roughly 47% of unit-level equity before fees and interest - it is not a valuation dispute. Per the standing taxonomy, valuation findings get a price gate; business-risk findings get a size cut, which from zero is zero. Do not write an alert_below for this name. A cheaper JBGS with the same tail is not a better JBGS.

ONE PROCESS NOTE THE DESK SHOULD NOT WAVE THROUGH. Both benches declared the DC Superior Court docket a coverage gap because CourtListener and RECAP are federal-only. That is true and correctly stated - but the desk has a standing capability for exactly this case: driving a real Chrome session past gated government portals, which is how the decisive AHC Bozeman source was obtained. DC Courts runs a public CaseSearch portal. The apportionment structure, the Rule 62 bond ruling and the post-judgment interest rate are all sitting behind it and none of the three was attempted. Declaring the gap is honest; declaring it when we own the tool is a process failure.
blue_ruling: SUSTAINED, one finding reduced. Blue verified red's decisive kill against the 10-Q contingencies note verbatim, downgraded one over-tagged presumption from CONFIRMED to PLAUSIBLE, and added two findings that strengthen red rather than soften it. The benches are concordant at equal conviction. This is the cleanest court in the batch.
reopen_gates: EVENT: a DC Superior Court Rule 62 order setting a supersedeas bond MATERIALLY BELOW the full judgment without requiring cash collateral. Rule 62 defaults to judgment plus costs and interest but expressly permits the court to 'fix a different amount or order security other than the bond ... for good cause.' This is the binding near-term liquidity question and it is UNDATED and NEAR - the appeal was noticed off a judgment entered 7/31.

DISCLOSURE: any insurance-recovery disclosure responding to the judgment. The contingencies note is currently silent, and on a construction-defect-plus-misrepresentation claim that silence is doing real work in the sizing.

EVENT: a dividend CUT that pre-clears the liquidity overhang WITHOUT the stock re-rating. That combination would mean the market has already absorbed the bad news and the cash is being redirected to the bond - the only configuration in which this becomes interesting.

LEGAL: appellate briefing establishing that the treble is severable and reviewable de novo. Base damages were $118.7M; stripping the treble is a distinct and materially more winnable question than overturning liability, and it is the only leg that changes the tail by a multiple.

PROCESS (not a name gate, but it must be closed before any re-court): pull the DC Superior Court docket via the real-Chrome path against the DC Courts CaseSearch portal - apportionment structure, joint-and-several language, the Rule 62 ruling, and the post-judgment interest rate. All four are load-bearing and all four are currently UNVERIFIED because a federal-only connector was used on a DC Superior Court case.
